key_insight: Grain-filter excimer crystallization of sputtered Si gives hydrogen-free single-crystal n- and p-FETs inside a stack: the fallback for Smart Cut's implanted hydrogen in I-11545.
killer_doubt: Grains are ~6 um apart with random orientation, so SA pairs must share a grain. Floating-body tiers hold only ~10-100 ms at 85 C and need litho on every tier.
decisive_experiment: On a 4-tier IGZO 1T1C coupon, sputter Si, laser-crystallize it and build in-grain CMOS SA pairs. Measure IGZO Vt and retention shift after laser shots, and pair offset sigma (go: <20 mV shift, <5 mV sigma).
prior_art: TU Delft (Ishihara) mu-Czochralski single-grain TFTs; TSRI/NARL laser-crystallized monolithic 3D; CEA-Leti nanosecond-laser sequential 3D. From memory.

key_insight: Put the coolant in the memory wafer of a memory-on-logic stack. The memory then sits ~0.5 K above the channel wall, so Si DRAM can survive on ~1 kW logic.
killer_doubt: At 125 W/cm2 with h~1e5 W/m2K, memory runs 13-30 K above coolant, worse over hot spots. Tail Ea of 0.3-0.6 eV gives 3-11x retention; refresh is ~10% of power.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the N-41 dossier: thin a commercial DRAM die, etch 150 um channels, bond it onto a 125 W/cm2 heater die, and map the retention tail against coolant temperature to extract tail Ea.
prior_art: IBM Zurich interlayer microchannel cooling of 3D stacks; Tuckerman-Pease 1981; Microsoft/Corintis in-chip microfluidics (2025); R18 dropped the cool-spec sled I-11571.

key_insight: Transistor-written oxide gain cells in the logic die's own BEOL: capacity-class memory at ~0.2 pJ/bit, with no extra wafer, no TSV and no write-endurance limit.
killer_doubt: Yield coupling: at 99% unrepairable yield per tier, 16 tiers lose 15% of $500+ logic dies. Each 3-bit level is only ~120 e- on a ~0.15 fF node at 105 C.
decisive_experiment: Deposit 2-4 vertical IGZO 2T0C tiers on finished 22-28 nm foundry logic die. Measure 3-bit retention and drift at 105 C over 1,000 h, plus logic Vt and ring-oscillator shift after the <=400 C flow.
prior_art: Stanford/MIT N3XT memory-on-logic; SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM in BEOL; imec IGZO 2T0C; Kioxia/Nanya OCTRAM. From memory.

key_insight: A nested bit-plane layout lets one stored copy also serve as a self-speculative draft, with no second model. A useful serving trick, but not a memory-supply lever.
killer_doubt: A 4-plane draft (50% of bytes) with k=4 and acceptance 0.85 needs ~0.81 weight bytes per token, ~1.2x. Two-plane drafts accept poorly, and batching already amortizes weight reads.
decisive_experiment: Software only: on a Matryoshka-quantized 8B model, measure the acceptance of 2- and 4-plane drafts in vLLM at batch 1-64. Go if >=1.5x tokens/s at batch 16.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024); Matryoshka Quantization (2025); QSpec quantized self-speculation (2024); R28 dropped the same idea as I-05807. From memory.

key_insight: Taking density from tiers rather than pitch lets imprint at F~100 nm on glass reach ~2x 1-beta per area. Self-contained mm-scale tiles avoid panel-scale overlay.
killer_doubt: No panel-size HAR etcher or conformal ALD exists; both are new $100M+ tools. Uncompensated, an 8 um, 200 MPa stack bows 0.7 mm glass ~13 mm over 620 mm.
decisive_experiment: On Gen-2 glass, deposit a stress-compensated 16-tier oxide/W stack, imprint 100 nm holes and etch them. Map bow, hole CD and depth from centre to edge. Go if CD 3-sigma <10%.
prior_art: Phase B N-38; SEL CAAC-IGZO; Canon NIL; large-area wire-grid imprint. Earlier verdicts: I-10785 ADVANCE, I-03879 DROP.

key_insight: Scoring on the MSB planes of the real INT8 keys avoids storing a duplicate sketch. KV capacity splits between a PIM tier and a cheaper tier.
killer_doubt: KIVI 2-bit KV already gives ~8x capacity in one tier. Fetching the top 2k tokens (~160 KB each for a 70B GQA model) is ~0.33 GB per sequence-step: ~5 ms over 64 GB/s CXL.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-09070 dossier: trace-driven 128k-context decode simulation (Ramulator plus an AttAcc model) of MSB-plane top-k on UPMEM or LPDDR5X-PIM, compared on tokens/s/$ with ShadowKV and KIVI-2bit.
prior_art: ShadowKV, Quest and InfiniGen top-k KV; SpAtten MSB-first fetch; AttAcc, HBM-PIM, AiM; R11 ADVANCE I-09070; R28 DROP I-03037. From memory.

key_insight: A 16-cell vertical bitline (~2-4 fF) decouples capacitor size from tier count. At EOT ~0.45 nm (~77 fF/um2), 0.3-0.6 fF fits a 30-60 nm lateral capacitor.
killer_doubt: Signal is ~0.5 V x 0.45/(0.45+3) ≈ 65 mV, which needs offset-cancelled SAs. Four Smart Cut c-Si layers (SOI donor plus a FEOL-lite pass each) may add ~$8-16k per wafer.
decisive_experiment: Build 4-tier IGZO 1T1C with 30-60 nm lateral caps and measure retention at 85 C. Then apply a 400 C bond/split thermal and hydrogen sequence with an Al2O3 barrier and remeasure (go: Vt drift <20 mV).
prior_art: CEA-Leti CoolCube 400 C sequential CMOS; layer-transfer DRAM patents; M3D DRAM periphery tier (arXiv 2008.11367). No interleaved SA layer found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Binary Vt-coded select pillars address N tiers with 2log2(N) gates instead of an N-step staircase: ~2.7 um rather than ~32 um at 64 tiers, which allows short 3D lines.
killer_doubt: The selected line crosses 12 series oxide pass devices at ~20 kOhm each: ~240 kOhm x 30 fF ≈ 7 ns per edge. Unselected tiers float unless a second coded pull-down path is added.
decisive_experiment: Build an 8-tier IGZO or poly-Si test stack with 6 coded select pillars plus complementary pull-down pillars. Measure selected-line RC, VPP pass-through loss and unselected-line coupling disturb at 85 C.
prior_art: Macronix VG-NAND layer select by multilevel operation (LSM, ~2011); NMOS depletion-mode ROM decoders; 3D NAND staircase-reduction work. From memory.

key_insight: Tier-granular sparing makes random tier defects yield-neutral at ~6% area. It is a design rule every 3D-memory dossier should carry, not a standalone invention.
killer_doubt: Separately built 8-tier groups need joins at bitline pitch (~40-80 nm) against a ~0.4-1 um hybrid-bond pitch. Eight carriers give up single-etch amortization, and test structures miss in-array defects.
decisive_experiment: Not as a standalone project. Inside the 3D dossiers, run Monte Carlo yield on per-tier killer densities measured from an 8-16-tier test stack, comparing sparing with grouping on cost per good bit.
prior_art: 3D NAND spare blocks, word lines and bad-block tables; DRAM row/column redundancy; HBM known-good-die stacking; R06 dropped the same sparing rule as I-02910.

key_insight: A vacuum barrier has no traps, SILC or charge-to-breakdown, so it is one of the few charge-write routes that could escape the charge-fluence endurance wall.
killer_doubt: Retention changes ~5x per 0.1 nm of gap at 2.7 eV, and TiN roughness of ~0.3-0.5 nm rms lets asperities dominate. IGZO 2T0C already gives >200 s retention with unlimited endurance.
decisive_experiment: Release 3 nm sacrificial-carbon gaps over amorphous-metal floating gates on ~1,000 MOSFETs at a university fab. Map the retention spread at 85 C and FN write cycling to 1e10. Go if 6-sigma spread <100x.
prior_art: NASA Ames vacuum-channel transistors; ALD-spacer nanogaps from atomic layer lithography (Oh group, 2013); NAND inter-cell air gaps. Vacuum-barrier floating-gate memory: none known (no search).

key_insight: Charge shifted through an oxide channel wears only the gate dielectric, and NAND-like tiers need no per-bit transistor or capacitor: the largest deposition-only density lever.
killer_doubt: imec's IGZO CCD reaches CTE >98%, but 128 transfers need >=0.9999 (0.98^128 keeps 7.5%). At imec's >4 MHz, a 64-stage shift takes ~16 us: buffer-class, not DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-10793 dossier: university planar 4-phase IGZO CCD lines of 128-256 gates, measuring per-transfer CTE against clock (4-100 MHz) and dark fill at 85 C. Go if >=0.9999 at >=20 MHz.
prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar IGZO CCD; imec IMW 2026 vertical 3D CCD (via search snippet, logged R16); 1970s Si CCD memories. Same card as R16's ADVANCE I-10793.

key_insight: Reuses DRAM's AR-65 hole as a bottom-up electroplating template for a 10-25-bit vertical shift register with wear-free magnetic writes and zero refresh.
killer_doubt: Under ~40 nm diameter, walls are transverse, not Bloch-point. Fast shifting needs ~3e11-1e12 A/m2 (100-300 uA at 20 nm) against ~30-60 uA from the select transistor. Shift errors below 1e-12 are unshown.
decisive_experiment: Pulse-electroplate Co/Ni-modulated wires into 20-40 nm oxide holes and contact single wires. Count shift errors over 1e9 pulses by MR readout against current density. Go if <1e-9 at <=1e11 A/m2.
prior_art: Parkin/IBM racetrack (2008); SPINTEC (Fruchart) and Vazquez-group modulated electroplated cylindrical wires; Bloch-point walls >600 m/s (Schobitz 2019). From memory.
